players.product: Data center leasing to hyperscalers and enterprises (Northern Virginia, Richmond, London, Amsterdam, Mumbai; ~325 MW of leasable capacity energizing over the next 24 months) plus hyperscale and neocloud data center decommissioning

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 supplemental financial information (8-K Exhibit 99.3), data center portfolio at June 30, 2026: leasable megawatts 528.5 (450.2 a year earlier), leased 97.1% in total and 97.4% of stabilized capacity, 31 facilities in 21 markets. Total potential capacity was 1,372.9 MW (1,279.9 MW a year earlier): 528.5 MW operating, 160.2 MW under construction and 684.2 MW held for development. The earnings presentation (Exhibit 99.2) says the build-out will increase capacity more than 2.5 times to 1.4 GW from the current operating portfolio of 529 MW. The data center customer lease expiration schedule totals 1,710 leases, 615.7 MW and $1,044,199 thousand of annualized GAAP TCV rent, with a weighted average lease expiration of 10.2 years; Q2 churn was 2.0%.
quarterly_data.figure: 528.5 leasable MW (97.1% leased); 160.2 MW under construction; 684.2 MW held for development; total 1,372.9 MW; WALE 10.2 years

quarterly_data.signal: Data center development and backlog (8-K Exhibits 99.2 and 99.3): of the 160.2 MW under construction, 114.0 MW (71.2%) is pre-leased, with $977.3 million invested to date and $1,449.1 million total expected investment. Pre-leased projects include Northern Virginia VA-9 Phase 1 (14.0 MW, 100% pre-leased, expected completion Q4 2026) and Phase 2 (14.0 MW, Q1 2027), Miami MIA-1 (16.0 MW, 100% pre-leased, Q4 2026) and Amsterdam AMS-1 Phase 4 (10.0 MW, 100% pre-leased, Q2 2027); London LON-3 future phases (25.0 MW, $391.9 million total expected investment) and Madrid MAD-2/3 (20.0 MW) are expected to complete in Q1 2027. The company says its current backlog, before any new leasing, is expected to drive data center growth of 25%+ in 2026, and as of June 30 supports an additional $370 million of growth beyond 2026, with the July leases adding to this.
quarterly_data.figure: 114.0 MW pre-leased (71.2%); $1,449.1 million total expected investment; backlog supports additional $370 million of growth beyond 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 leasing and capex detail (8-K Exhibit 99.3): new/expansion data center leases signed in Q2 totalled 13,127 kW at $205 per kW per month (34,976 kW at $199 year to date), commenced leases 24,509 kW, and cash / GAAP renewal mark-to-market 11.8% / 13.8%. Data center growth capital expenditures were $472,002 thousand in Q2 2026, up 25.2% from $376,983 thousand, within total growth capital expenditures of $552,764 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: 13,127 kW signed at $205/kW/month; Q2 data center growth capex $472,002 thousand (+25.2%)
